paite: Ka kiang ah TOUPA thu hong tung a, ka kiang ah,
heading: Tura Vuina La
english: Yahweh’s word came again to me, saying,

paite: "Nang, mihing tapa, Tura kho suunna la phuak inla,
english: “You, son of man, take up a lamentation over Tyre;

paite: Tura khua kiang ah, Aw nang tuipi gei a teng sek, tuipi gei gam tampite kiang a sumsin, Toupa PATHIAN in huchi in ahon chi: Aw nang Tura, ka kilawm bukim na chi maw;
english: and tell Tyre, ‘You who dwell at the entry of the sea, who are the merchant of the peoples to many islands, the Lord Yahweh says: “You, Tyre, have said, ‘I am perfect in beauty.’

paite: "Na gam in tuipi lai asun hi, nang hon bawlte'n hon kilawm tungtuansak mah ve ua;
english: Your borders are in the heart of the seas. Your builders have perfected your beauty.

paite: Na singzat Senir meilah in abawl ua; na longpeu ding in, Lebanon a sidar in abawl uhi;
english: They have made all your planks of cypress trees from Senir. They have taken a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you.

paite: Bashan tosaw na longzapna ding in abawl ua; saiha suangphum na long pialkhang ding in, taksing tuipi gam Kupra a kipan in.
english: They have made your oars of the oaks of Bashan. They have made your benches of ivory inlaid in cypress wood from the islands of Kittim.

paite: Na long puanzak Aigupta puanmalngat gial, nang chiamtehna ding in ana tung hi, nang a dia limzak dumpuang, sandup, Elishah tui gei a kipan;
english: Your sail was of fine linen with embroidered work from Egypt, that it might be to you for a banner. Blue and purple from the islands of Elishah was your awning.

paite: Na longkalmi Sidon, Arvad mi ahi; na long hawl mite leng Zemir misiamte ahi ua;
english: The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were your rowers. Your wise men, Tyre, were in you. They were your pilots.

paite: Gebal upa leh mikhutsiam, na long bulhtuah mite ahi ua, tuipi long teng leh amite'n, nang hong dawr ding in ahong zuan uhi.
english: The old men of Gebal and its wise men were your repairers of ship seams in you. All the ships of the sea with their mariners were in you to deal in your merchandise.

paite: "Na galdoumi, na sepaihhon, Persia, Lud, Put mite ahi ua, alum uh leh adal lukhu uh na baang ah akhai ua, nang kilawmsakte ahi uhi.
english: “‘“Persia, Lud, and Put were in your army, your men of war. They hung the shield and helmet in you. They showed your beauty.

paite: Na sepaihhon leh Arvad mite'n na kulhpi kimvel in aveng ua, Gammadim mite'n na insang aveng ua, alum uh na kulhpi kimvel in akhai ua, nang kilawmsakte ahi uhi.
english: The men of Arvad with your army were on your walls all around, and valiant men were in your towers. They hung their shields on your walls all around. They have perfected your beauty.

paite: Na hauh ziak in, sum-le-pai gou thil chiteng, Tarshish nang hon dawr mi ahong hi a, na van lei in ahon lam hi, dangkasik, sik, langva leh asuante leng.
english: “‘“Tarshish was your merchant by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches. They traded for your wares with silver, iron, tin, and lead.

paite: Zavan, Tubal, Meshek, nang hon dawrte'n sal leh dal tui-um belsuan in ahon dawr ua, na van neihna ding in.
english: “‘“Javan, Tubal, and Meshech were your traders. They traded the persons of men and vessels of bronze for your merchandise.

paite: Togarmah a mite'n sakol, kidouna sakol leh sabiltung in na van alei uhi.
english: “‘“They of the house of Togarmah traded for your wares with horses, war horses, and mules.

paite: Dedan mite nang hon dawr mite ahi ua, tui gei mun chih na sumsinna mun ahong hi a, saiha leh eboni ahon puak uhi.
english: “‘“The men of Dedan traded with you. Many islands were the market of your hand. They brought you horns of ivory and ebony in exchange.

paite: Van na hauh ziak in, Edom nang hon dawr ahong hi a, emerald suang, puan sandup, puanzep, puanmalngat, khibah, agate suangte in nang ahon dawr uh.
english: “‘“Syria was your merchant by reason of the multitude of your handiworks. They traded for your wares with emeralds, purple, embroidered work, fine linen, coral, and rubies.

paite: Judah leh Israel teng nang hon dawrte ahi ua, Minnith buh leh Pannag, khuaizu, sathau leh singnai in ahon dawr uh.
english: “‘“Judah and the land of Israel were your traders. They traded wheat of Minnith, confections, honey, oil, and balm for your merchandise.

paite: Na hauh ziak in, sum-le-pai gou thil chiteng, Damaskas nang hon dawr ahong hi a, Helbon uain leh belam mulkaang in ahon dawr hi.
english: “‘“Damascus was your merchant for the multitude of your handiworks by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches, with the wine of Helbon, and white wool.

paite: Uzal uain hon tawi in alei ua, na vante, sikseksa, singguithak leh kawltute na sumsinna.
english: “‘“Vedan and Javan traded with yarn for your wares; wrought iron, cassia, and calamus were among your merchandise.

paite: Dedan in sakol tungphah puante in nang ahon dawr hi.
english: “‘“Dedan was your merchant in precious saddle blankets for riding.

paite: Arabia leh Kedar kumpipate nang hon dawrte ahi vek uh, belamnoute, belamtalte, keltalte in ahon dawr uh.
english: “‘“Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your favorite dealers in lambs, rams, and goats. In these, they were your merchants.

paite: Sheba leh Raamah sumsin mite nang hon dawrte ahong hi ua, gimlim hoihpente, suangmantam chi chih leh dangka-engte in, nang ahon dawr uh.
english: “‘“The traders of Sheba and Raamah were your traders. They traded for your wares with the best of all spices, all precious stones, and gold.

paite: Haran, Kanneh leh Eden, Sheba, Assuria leh Kilmad sumsin mite nang hon dawrte ahi uh.
english: “‘“Haran, Canneh, Eden, the traders of Sheba, Asshur and Chilmad, were your traders.

paite: Huaite ahi uh, nang hon dawr, puansilh hoih chi, puandum buang, puanzep, pialkhang phah ze kilawm toh, khauhual chiptak a hek in, hiaite in nang ahon dawr uh.
english: These were your traders in choice wares, in wrappings of blue and embroidered work, and in cedar chests of rich clothing bound with cords, among your merchandise.

paite: "Tarshish longhon leh long lian vanpote ahi ua, na hong inbul in tuipi tung ah na hong thupita hi.
english: “‘“The ships of Tarshish were your caravans for your merchandise. You were replenished and made very glorious in the heart of the seas.

paite: Na long hawlpa'n tuipi kihot ah ahon hawllut a, suahlam huih in nang ahon nuaimang, tuipi lai ah.
english: Your rowers have brought you into great waters. The east wind has broken you in the heart of the seas.

paite: Na hauhsakna, na van, na sumsinna thil, na long mite, long hawlmi, bulhtuak mite, sumsin van kheng mite, na galbawl mite tengteng, nang a om, na sung a om teng- teng toh, na siat ni in tuipi lai ah na tummang ding uh.
english: Your riches, your wares, your merchandise, your mariners, your pilots, your repairers of ship seams, the dealers in your merchandise, and all your men of war who are in you, with all your company which is among you, will fall into the heart of the seas in the day of your ruin.

paite: Na long hawl mite kikou husa in na kim a mite aling uhi.
english: At the sound of the cry of your pilots, the pasture lands will shake.

paite: Longkalhna peu len mite tengteng, long mite leh, tuipi a hawl mite tengteng paisuk in, luipiau ah adingh uh.
english: All who handle the oars, the mariners and all the pilots of the sea, will come down from their ships. They will stand on the land,

paite: Na tungthu ah a-aw uh zak tham in asuah ding ua, khasetak in akap ding ua; alu ua leivuite buak in, vut lak ah akitholh ding uh.
english: and will cause their voice to be heard over you, and will cry bitterly. They will cast up dust on their heads. They will wallow in the ashes.

paite: Nang ziak in kimetgiau in, sai-ip puan ateng ding ua; khase lua in nakpitak a kap in nang ahon suun ding uh.
english: They will make themselves bald for you, and clothe themselves with sackcloth. They will weep for you in bitterness of soul, with bitter mourning.

paite: Nang hon suun in kahla asam ding ua, nang suun in Tura bang khopi kua a-om a, amah tuipi lai ah, adai sipsip hi.
english: In their wailing they will take up a lamentation for you, and lament over you, saying, ‘Who is there like Tyre, like her who is brought to silence in the middle of the sea?’

paite: Na vante'n tuipi a pan pawt in mi tampi avak kham sek; na dangka leh na van in lei kumpipate na hausak hi.
english: When your wares came from the seas, you filled many peoples. You enriched the kings of the earth with the multitude of your riches and of your merchandise.

paite: Tuipi thuk a na siat ni in, na sumsinna thil, na mite, nang toh athelthang uhi.
english: In the time that you were broken by the seas, in the depths of the waters, your merchandise and all your company fell within you.

paite: "Tui gei a teng mi tengteng in mulkimhuai ahon sa ua; akumpipate uh lau in asibup ua, amel uh alamdang hial hi.
english: All the inhabitants of the islands are astonished at you, and their kings are horribly afraid. They are troubled in their face.

paite: Mite lak a sumsin mite'n nang ahon khoisatkhum ua, mite a ding in launa na hong suakta a, na kilang ngei nawn kei ding, chi in ahon kahkhum uhi."
english: The merchants among the peoples hiss at you. You have come to a terrible end, and you will be no more.”’”
